summary.text: Molecular biology is the branch of biology that studies the molecular structures and chemical processes behind biological activity inside and between cells.
It centers largely on nucleic acids such as DNA and RNA and on proteins, and on how these macromolecules carry out replication, transcription and translation.
Its techniques are used to target new drugs, diagnose disease, and better understand how cells work.

items.prompt: A lab measures the purines in a DNA sample (adenine plus guanine). What should the pyrimidines (cytosine plus thymine) total?

options.label: About half as much as the purines
Double the purines
The same amount as the purines
Nothing, since they occur only in RNA

items.explain: Chargaff found that the total concentration of purines is always equal to that of pyrimidines.

items.prompt: A stretch of a gene's DNA is 12 bases long, read from a fixed start with no overlap, and codes for part of a protein. How many amino acids does it specify?

options.label: Four amino acids
Twelve amino acids
Six amino acids
Three amino acids

items.explain: Each triplet of bases (a codon) specifies one amino acid, and codons do not overlap, so 12 bases give 4.

items.prompt: Researchers tag a virus's protein coat with one radioactive marker and its genetic material with another, then let it infect bacteria. What did this show?

options.label: The protein coat carried all the instructions for making new viruses
The bacteria supplied the instructions and the virus supplied none
Coat and genetic material were equally needed to make new viruses
The genetic material injected held everything needed to make new viruses

items.explain: Hershey and Chase showed the DNA injected by a phage contains all the information needed to make progeny phage.

items.prompt: Cells were seen under microscopes in the 1700s, yet how they work at the molecular level stayed unclear for two centuries. What finally changed?

options.label: Biologists dropped whole organisms and began studying only single cells
Tools from physics and chemistry advanced enough to be used on biology problems
A new law of inheritance was found in pea plants
Cells were seen for the very first time under a microscope

items.explain: Detailed understanding of cell mechanisms arrived in the 20th century once physics and chemistry technologies could be applied to biology.

items.prompt: A biochemist studies pus-filled bandages and isolates a phosphorus-containing substance he calls nuclein. What do we now know it to be?

options.label: A protein from bacteria
A sugar capsule
A fat-like wax
DNA

items.explain: Friedrich Miescher's nuclein is now known to be DNA.

items.prompt: Why does a host's immune system fail against smooth-strain pneumococcus but beat the rough strain?

options.label: The rough strain's capsule makes it far easier for the host to attack
The smooth strain lacks any coat, so the immune system overlooks it
The smooth strain's polysaccharide capsule keeps the immune system from recognizing it
The rough strain makes antigens that smooth strains cannot produce

items.explain: The polysaccharide capsule hides smooth bacteria from the immune system, while the capsule-free rough strain is readily recognized and destroyed.
